title: Prove the defensive change, not merely the attack
description: Choose a technique, then record each independently verifiable artifact. A result closes only after the changed control survives an authorized replay.

stages.label: Execution authorized
stages.evidence: The operator records the approved command, target, time window, and stop condition.

stages.label: Telemetry captured
stages.evidence: The endpoint event contains the process lineage and encoded-command indicator expected by the test.

stages.label: Analytic fired
stages.evidence: The intended detection creates one attributable alert with the relevant entity and timestamp.

stages.label: Response performed
stages.evidence: The analyst follows the runbook and isolates only the authorized endpoint.

stages.label: Control retested
stages.evidence: The same test is replayed after the rule or runbook change and the expected behavior is observed.

stages.label: Execution authorized
stages.evidence: The change is limited to a disposable identity and a documented sandbox account.

stages.label: Telemetry captured
stages.evidence: The audit record identifies the actor, target principal, role, request ID, and source context.

stages.label: Analytic fired
stages.evidence: The policy-change analytic raises an alert before the agreed detection deadline.

stages.label: Response performed
stages.evidence: The responder verifies intent, revokes the grant, and preserves the relevant audit evidence.

stages.label: Control retested
stages.evidence: A second authorized grant proves the revised analytic and response path without touching production identities.

scenarios.label: Suspicious sign-in sequence
scenarios.technique: Valid Accounts with anomalous location context

stages.label: Execution authorized
stages.evidence: Two controlled sign-ins use the dedicated identity, approved egress points, and a bounded time window.

stages.label: Telemetry captured
stages.evidence: Both sign-ins carry identity, location, device, session, and authentication context.

stages.label: Analytic fired
stages.evidence: The identity-risk policy links the events and creates an attributable case rather than two unrelated alerts.

stages.label: Response performed
stages.evidence: The workflow challenges the identity and invalidates only the test sessions.

stages.label: Control retested
stages.evidence: The controlled sequence is repeated after tuning to verify detection without blocking the approved baseline sign-in.
